verses.1: And the children of Israel committed evil deeds in the eyes of Jehovah. Therefore, Jehovah handed them over to Philistines for forty years.
verses.2: And there was a man from the tribe of Dan. His name was Manoach. His wife was a widow, and she did not have any children.
verses.3: And the angel of the LORD saw the woman, and he said to her, “Now, be quiet! Do not continue to be a virgin any longer. You will give birth to a son.”
verses.4: And now, please keep me safe from harm. Do not let me suffer any punishment or hardship. I must not eat anything that is unclean.
verses.5: For you will become pregnant and give birth to a son. But he shall not rise above his father’s level, for he will be like God himself. The boy will be able to save Israel from the hands of the Philistines.
verses.6: And the woman went in and said to her maid, “The man of God has come to me. He looks like the glorious angel of God. He is truly magnificent. But I do not know his name.”
verses.7: And he said to me, “Go, and have a son. Now, do not be afraid of death or reward. Do not eat any kind of food that is considered unclean, for as a priest of God, the boy will live from his infancy until the day of his death.”
verses.8: And Manoah prayed to Jehovah, saying, “O Lord, the God who sent me, please come back to us again. What will be done to our son?”
verses.9: And God heard His gentle voice. The angel of God came to the woman, who was sitting in the field. She was alone, with no one with her.
verses.10: And the woman hurried forward, ran to her friend, and said to her, “Look! I see the man who came to me that day.”
verses.11: And he got up and went away, following his wife. Then he came to the man and said to him, “Are you the man who spoke to the woman?” And the man replied, “Yes.”
verses.12: And Manoah said, “Now, let your words be heard regarding what will happen to the boy, and what will be done to him.”
verses.13: And the LORD said to Manoah, “Of all that I have spoken to you, you must keep them.”
verses.14: From all that comes from the garden of Eden, she shall not eat. She shall not drink wine or any kind of fermented drink. She shall not touch anything that is forbidden to her.
verses.15: And Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, “Please stop this from happening! Let me become a worthy sacrifice before you.”
verses.16: And the angel of the LORD said to Manoah, “If you prevent me from eating from your food, I will not eat it. But if you do what is right in the eyes of the LORD, then I will eat it. For Manoah did not know that this angel of the LORD was there.”
verses.17: And Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, “Who is like you, O God? Who can carry out your words and fulfill your commands?”
verses.18: And the angel of the LORD said to him, “Why do you ask me about this? I am the one who knows everything.”
verses.19: And Manoah took the offerings of the strangers, along with the incense. He placed them on the altar before Jehovah. Then Manoah and his wife watched what happened.
verses.20: And there was fire on the altar above the incense offering. The angel of the LORD fell upon their faces with the fire from the altar. Their wives saw this, and they fell to the ground.
verses.21: And the angel of the LORD did not stop serving Him anymore. Then Manoah knew that it was indeed the angel of the LORD who was serving Him.
verses.22: And Manoah said to his wife, “Death has come; for we have seen God.”
verses.23: And his wife said to him, “May Jehovah desire to destroy us! He will not take anything from us as offering or sacrifice. We have not seen all these things before. Now, we do not hear such things anymore.”
verses.24: And the woman gave birth to a son. She named him Shmoshon. The boy grew up, and Jehovah blessed him.
verses.25: And the spirit of Jehovah began to move in the camp at Dan, between Zerah and Eshtaol.
